title: The Largest Star in the Universe – Size Comparison

blocks.en_text: What is the largest star in the universe?
blocks.zh_text: 宇宙中最大的恒星是什么？

blocks.en_text: And why is it that large?
blocks.zh_text: 它为什么那么大？

blocks.en_text: And what are stars anyway?
blocks.zh_text: 恒星到底是什么？

blocks.en_text: Things that would like to be stars
blocks.zh_text: 那些想成为恒星的天体

blocks.en_text: We begin our journey with Earth.
blocks.zh_text: 我们从地球开始这段旅程。

blocks.en_text: Not to learn anything,
blocks.zh_text: 不是为了学到什么，

blocks.en_text: Just to get a vague sense of scale.
blocks.zh_text: 只是为了对尺度有个模糊的感觉。

blocks.en_text: The smallest things that have some star like properties
blocks.zh_text: 那些具有某些类似恒星特性的最小天体

blocks.en_text: are large gas giants or sub-brown dwarfs.
blocks.zh_text: 是巨大的气态巨行星或亚褐矮星。

blocks.en_text: Like Jupiter,
blocks.zh_text: 比如木星，

blocks.en_text: the most massive planet in the solar system.
blocks.zh_text: 太阳系中质量最大的行星。

blocks.en_text: 11 times larger and 317 times more massive than Earth,
blocks.zh_text: 体积是地球的11倍，质量是地球的317倍，

blocks.en_text: and more or less made of the same stuff as our sun.
blocks.zh_text: 而且构成它的物质跟我们太阳的差不多。

blocks.en_text: Just much, much less of it.
blocks.zh_text: 只是量少得多得多。

blocks.en_text: The transition toward stars begins with been dwarfs,
blocks.zh_text: 向恒星的过渡始于褐矮星，

blocks.en_text: failed stars that are a huge disappointment to their mums.
blocks.zh_text: 这些失败的恒星让它们的妈妈大失所望。

blocks.en_text: They have between 13 and 90 times the mass of Jupiter.
blocks.zh_text: 它们的质量是木星的13到90倍。

blocks.en_text: So even if we took 90 Jupiters, and threw them at each other,
blocks.zh_text: 所以即使我们拿90个木星，把它们互相扔在一起，

blocks.en_text: although fun to watch, it wouldn't be enough to create a star.
blocks.zh_text: 虽然看着挺好玩，但也不足以创造出一颗恒星。

blocks.en_text: Interestingly, adding lots of mass to a brown dwarf doesn't make it much bigger,
blocks.zh_text: 有趣的是，给褐矮星增加大量质量并不会让它大多少，

blocks.en_text: just it's insides denser.
blocks.zh_text: 只会让它的内部更致密。

blocks.en_text: This increases the pressure in the core enough, to make certain nuclear reactions happen slowly,
blocks.zh_text: 这会让核心的压力增大到足以让某些核反应缓慢发生，

blocks.en_text: and the object glow a little.
blocks.zh_text: 并让这个天体微微发光。

blocks.en_text: So brown dwarfs are a sort of glowy gas giant
blocks.zh_text: 所以褐矮星算是一种会发光的气态巨行星，

blocks.en_text: that don't fit into any category very well.
blocks.zh_text: 很难归入任何一个类别。

blocks.en_text: But we want to talk about stars not failed wannabe stars, so let's move on.
blocks.zh_text: 但我们想聊的是恒星，不是失败的准恒星，所以继续往下看吧。

blocks.en_text: Main sequence stars
blocks.zh_text: 主序星

blocks.en_text: Once large gas balls pass a certain mass threshold,
blocks.zh_text: 一旦巨大的气体球超过某个质量阈值，

blocks.en_text: their core become hot and sense enough to ignite.
blocks.zh_text: 它们的核心就会变得足够热、足够致密，从而被点燃。

blocks.en_text: Hydrogen is fuss to helium in their cores, releasing tremendous amounts of energy.
blocks.zh_text: 核心中的氢聚变成氦，释放出巨大的能量。

blocks.en_text: Stars that do that, are called main sequence stars.
blocks.zh_text: 这样做的恒星被称为主序星。

blocks.en_text: The more massive a main sequence star is, the hotter and brighter it burns, and the shorter its life is.
blocks.zh_text: 主序星的质量越大，燃烧得就越热、越亮，寿命也越短。

blocks.en_text: Once the hydrogen burning phase is over, stars grow,
blocks.zh_text: 一旦氢燃烧阶段结束，恒星就会膨胀，

blocks.en_text: Up to hundreds of thousand of times their original size.
blocks.zh_text: 最多能膨胀到原来体积的几十万倍。

blocks.en_text: But these giant phases only last for a fraction of their lifespan.
blocks.zh_text: 但这些巨星阶段只占它们寿命的一小部分。

blocks.en_text: So we'll be comparing stars at drastically different stages in their lives.
blocks.zh_text: 所以我们要比较的恒星，处于它们生命中截然不同的阶段。

blocks.en_text: This doesn't make them less impressive,
blocks.zh_text: 这并不会让它们逊色，

blocks.en_text: But maybe it's good to keep in mind that we'll be comparing babies to adults.
blocks.zh_text: 但也许最好记住，我们是在拿婴儿和成年人作比较。

blocks.en_text: Now, back to the beginning.
blocks.zh_text: 现在，回到最开始。

blocks.en_text: The smallest real star, are red dwarfs, about 100 times the mass of Jupiter,
blocks.zh_text: 最小的真正恒星是红矮星，质量约为木星的100倍，

blocks.en_text: Barely massive enough to fuse hydrogen to helium.
blocks.zh_text: 勉强有足够的质量把氢聚变成氦。

blocks.en_text: Because they're not very massive, they are small, not very hot and shine pretty dimly.
blocks.zh_text: 因为它们质量不大，所以个头小、温度不高，发出的光也相当暗淡。

blocks.en_text: They are the only stars in the main sequence that don't grow when they die
blocks.zh_text: 它们是主序星中唯一在死亡时不会膨胀的恒星，

blocks.en_text: but sort of... fizz out.
blocks.zh_text: 而是有点……慢慢熄灭。

blocks.en_text: Red dwarfs are by far the most abundant type [of stars] in the universe
blocks.zh_text: 红矮星是宇宙中数量最多的一类恒星，

blocks.en_text: Because they burn their fuel very slowly, it lasts them up to ten trillion years,
blocks.zh_text: 因为它们燃烧燃料非常缓慢，所以能持续燃烧长达十万亿年，

blocks.en_text: a thousand times the current age of the universe.
blocks.zh_text: 是宇宙当前年龄的一千倍。

blocks.en_text: For example, one of the closest stars to Earth is a red dwarf star, Barnard's star.
blocks.zh_text: 比如，离地球最近的恒星之一就是一颗红矮星——巴纳德星。

blocks.en_text: shines too dimly to be seen without a telescope
blocks.zh_text: 它发出的光太暗，不用望远镜根本看不见。

blocks.en_text: We made a whole video on red dwarfs if you want to learn more.
blocks.zh_text: 如果你想了解更多，我们专门做过一整期关于红矮星的视频。

blocks.en_text: The next stage are stars like our sun.
blocks.zh_text: 下一个阶段是像我们太阳这样的恒星。

blocks.en_text: To say the sun dominates the solar system is not doing it justice,
blocks.zh_text: 说太阳主宰着太阳系，都还不足以形容它的地位，

blocks.en_text: since it makes up 99.6% of all it's mass.
blocks.zh_text: 因为它占了太阳系总质量的99.6%。

blocks.en_text: It burns far hotter and brighter than red dwarfs which reduced its lifetime to about 10 billion years.
blocks.zh_text: 它燃烧的温度和亮度都远高于红矮星，这使它的寿命缩短到大约100亿年。

blocks.en_text: The sun is 7 times more massive than Barnard's star,
blocks.zh_text: 太阳的质量是巴纳德星的7倍，

blocks.en_text: but that makes it nearly 300 times brighter, with twice it's surface temperature.
blocks.zh_text: 但它的亮度却高出近300倍，表面温度也是后者的两倍。

blocks.en_text: Let's go bigger.
blocks.zh_text: 咱们往更大的看。

blocks.en_text: Small changes in mass produce enormous changes in a main sequence star's brightness.
blocks.zh_text: 质量的微小变化，会让主序星的亮度发生巨大的变化。

blocks.en_text: The brightest star in the night sky, Sirius A, is two solar masses, with a radius 1.7 times that of the sun.
blocks.zh_text: 夜空中最亮的恒星天狼星A，质量是太阳的两倍，半径是太阳的1.7倍。

blocks.en_text: But it's surface is nearly 10,000℃, making it shine 25 times brighter.
blocks.zh_text: 但它的表面温度接近10000℃，所以亮度是太阳的25倍。

blocks.en_text: Burning that hot reduces it's total lifespan by 4 times, to 2.5 billion years.
blocks.zh_text: 燃烧得这么热，使它的总寿命缩短了4倍，只有25亿年。

blocks.en_text: Stars close to ten times the mass of our sun have surface temperatures near 25,000℃.
blocks.zh_text: 质量接近太阳十倍的恒星，表面温度接近25000℃。

blocks.en_text: Beta Centauri contains two of these massive stars, each shining with about 20,000 times the power of the sun.
blocks.zh_text: 半人马座β包含两颗这样的大质量恒星，每颗的亮度大约是太阳的两万倍。

blocks.en_text: That's a lot of power, coming from something only 13 times larger [than the sun].
blocks.zh_text: 这能量可真不少，而它们的体积只比太阳大13倍。

blocks.en_text: But they'll only burn for about 20 million years
blocks.zh_text: 但它们只能燃烧大约2000万年，

blocks.en_text: Entire generations of these blue stars die in the time it takes the sun to orbit the Galaxy
blocks.zh_text: 太阳绕银河系转一圈的时间里，这些蓝色恒星就已经整整好几代生灭更替了。

blocks.en_text: So is this the formula?
blocks.zh_text: 那么规律就是这样吗？

blocks.en_text: The more massive, the larger the star.
blocks.zh_text: 质量越大，恒星就越大。

blocks.en_text: The most massive star that we know is R136a1.
blocks.zh_text: 我们知道的质量最大的恒星是R136a1。

blocks.en_text: It has 315 solar masses, and is nearly 9 million times brighter than the sun.
blocks.zh_text: 它有315个太阳质量，亮度接近太阳的900万倍。

blocks.en_text: And yet, despite its tremendous mass and power, it's barely 30 times the size of the sun.
blocks.zh_text: 然而，尽管它有着巨大的质量和能量，它的体积却只有太阳的30倍左右。

blocks.en_text: The star is so extreme and barely held together by gravity that it loses
blocks.zh_text: 这颗恒星极端到几乎无法靠引力维系自身，以至于它会流失

blocks.en_text: 321 thousand billion tonnes of material through its stellar wind.
blocks.zh_text: 321万亿吨的物质，通过它的恒星风。

blocks.en_text: Every single second.
blocks.zh_text: 每一秒都如此。

blocks.en_text: Stars of this sort are extremely rare because they break the rules of star formation a tiny bit.
blocks.zh_text: 这类恒星极其罕见，因为它们稍微打破了恒星形成的规律。

blocks.en_text: When supermassive stars are born, they burn extremely hot and bright,
blocks.zh_text: 当超大质量恒星诞生时，它们燃烧得极其炽热明亮，

blocks.en_text: and this blows away any extra gas that could make them more massive.
blocks.zh_text: 这会把任何能让它们变得更重的多余气体吹走。

blocks.en_text: So the mass limit for such a star is around 150 times the sun
blocks.zh_text: 所以这类恒星的质量上限大约是太阳的150倍。

blocks.en_text: Stars like R136a1 are probably formed through the merging of several high mass stars
blocks.zh_text: 像R136a1这样的恒星，很可能是由几颗大质量恒星合并而成的，

blocks.en_text: in dense star forming regions, and burn their core hydrogen in only a few million years.
blocks.zh_text: 在密集的恒星形成区里，它们只用几百万年就烧尽核心的氢。

blocks.en_text: So this means they are rare and short lived.
blocks.zh_text: 所以这意味着它们既稀有又短命。

blocks.en_text: From here, the trick to growing bigger isn't adding more mass,
blocks.zh_text: 到了这一步，变得更大的诀窍并不是增加更多质量，

blocks.en_text: To make the biggest stars, we have to kill them.
blocks.zh_text: 要造出最大的恒星，我们得先杀死它们。

blocks.en_text: Red giants
blocks.zh_text: 红巨星

blocks.en_text: When main sequence stars begins to exhaust the hydrogen in their core,
blocks.zh_text: 当主序星开始耗尽核心的氢时，

blocks.en_text: It contracts, making it hotter and denser.
blocks.zh_text: 核心会收缩，变得更热、更致密。

blocks.en_text: This leads to hotter do faster fusion, which pushes back against gravity,
blocks.zh_text: 这导致更热、更快的聚变，从而抵抗引力，

blocks.en_text: and makes tee outer layer swell, in a giant phase.
blocks.zh_text: 并使外层膨胀，进入巨星阶段。

blocks.en_text: And these stars become truly giant indeed.
blocks.zh_text: 而这些恒星确实变得非常巨大。

blocks.en_text: For example Gacrux, only 30% more massive than the sun,
blocks.zh_text: 比如Gacrux，质量只比太阳大30%，

blocks.en_text: It has swollen to about 84 times it's radius.
blocks.zh_text: 它却膨胀到了大约自身半径的84倍。

blocks.en_text: Still, when the sun enters the last stage of its life, it will swell and become even bigger.
blocks.zh_text: 不过，当太阳进入生命的最后阶段时，它也会膨胀，变得更大。

blocks.en_text: 200 times its current radius.
blocks.zh_text: 达到它目前半径的200倍。

blocks.en_text: In this final phase of its life, it will swallow the inner planets.
blocks.zh_text: 在生命的最后阶段，它会吞没内行星。

blocks.en_text: And if you think that's impressive, let's finally introduce the largest stars in the universe
blocks.zh_text: 如果你觉得这已经很惊人了，那我们终于要介绍宇宙中最大的恒星了。

blocks.en_text: Hypergiants
blocks.zh_text: 超巨星

blocks.en_text: Hypergiants are the giant phase of the most massive stars in the universe.
blocks.zh_text: 超巨星是宇宙中质量最大的恒星所处的巨星阶段。

blocks.en_text: They have an enormous surface area that can radiate an insane amount of light.
blocks.zh_text: 它们有着巨大的表面积，能辐射出多得离谱的光。

blocks.en_text: Being so large, They're basically blowing themselves apart, as gravity at the surface is too weak
blocks.zh_text: 由于如此巨大，它们基本上是在把自己吹散，因为表面的引力太弱，

blocks.en_text: to hold on to the hot mass which is lifted away in powerful stellar winds.
blocks.zh_text: 无法留住那些被强大的恒星风吹走的热物质。

blocks.en_text: Pistol star is 25 solar masses, but 300 times the radius of the sun,
blocks.zh_text: 手枪星有25个太阳质量，但半径是太阳的300倍，

blocks.en_text: a blue hypergiant, aptly named for its energetic bye star light.
blocks.zh_text: 它是一颗蓝色超巨星，这个名字恰如其分地来自它那充满能量的星光。

blocks.en_text: It's hard to say exactly how long pistol star will live, but probably just a few million years.
blocks.zh_text: 很难说手枪星到底能活多久，但大概也就几百万年。

blocks.en_text: Even larger than the blue hypergiants, are the yellow hypergiants.
blocks.zh_text: 比蓝超巨星更大的，是黄超巨星。

blocks.en_text: The most well studied is Rho Cassiopeiae, a star so bright
blocks.zh_text: 研究得最透彻的是仙后座ρ星，这颗星非常明亮，

blocks.en_text: it can be seen with the naked eye although it's thousand of light years from Earth.
blocks.zh_text: 虽然它距离地球有几千光年，但用肉眼就能看见。

blocks.en_text: At 40 solar masses, this star is about 500 times the radius of the sun and 500,000 times brighter.
blocks.zh_text: 这颗星有40个太阳质量，半径约为太阳的500倍，亮度是太阳的50万倍。

blocks.en_text: If the Earth was as close to Rho Cassiopeiae as it is to the sun,
blocks.zh_text: 如果地球和仙后座ρ星的距离，跟地球到太阳的距离一样近，

blocks.en_text: It would be inside it, and you would be very dead.
blocks.zh_text: 那地球就会在它内部，而你早就死透了。

blocks.en_text: Yellow hypergiants are very rare though.
blocks.zh_text: 不过黄超巨星非常罕见。

blocks.en_text: Only 15 are known.
blocks.zh_text: 目前已知的只有15颗。

blocks.en_text: This means they're likely just a short-lived intermediate state,
blocks.zh_text: 这意味着它们很可能只是一个短暂的中间状态，

blocks.en_text: as a star grows or shrinks between other phases of hypergiantness.
blocks.zh_text: 是恒星在超巨星的不同阶段之间变大或变小时的样子。

blocks.en_text: With red hypergiants, we can reach the largest stars known to us,
blocks.zh_text: 说到红超巨星，我们就触及了已知最大的恒星，

blocks.en_text: probably the largest stars even possible.
blocks.zh_text: 可能也是恒星能达到的最大尺寸。

blocks.en_text: So who's the winner of this insane contest?
blocks.zh_text: 那么这场疯狂的比拼，谁才是赢家呢？

blocks.en_text: Well, the truth is we don't know.
blocks.zh_text: 其实，我们也不知道。

blocks.en_text: Red hypergiants are extremely bright and far away, which means even tiny uncertainties in our measurements
blocks.zh_text: 红超巨星极其明亮又极其遥远，这意味着哪怕我们的测量只有一点点不确定，

blocks.en_text: can give us a huge margin of error for their size.
blocks.zh_text: 算出来的尺寸误差也会非常大。

blocks.en_text: Worse still, red hypergiants are solar system size behemoths that are blowing themselves apart,
blocks.zh_text: 更糟的是，红超巨星是太阳系级别的庞然大物，还在不断把自己吹散，

blocks.en_text: which makes them harder to measure.
blocks.zh_text: 这让它们更难测量。

blocks.en_text: As we do more science and our instruments improve, whatever the largest star is change.
blocks.zh_text: 随着我们做更多研究、仪器不断进步，所谓最大的恒星也会变。

blocks.en_text: The star that is currently thought to be among the largest we've found is Stevenson 2-18.
blocks.zh_text: 目前被认为是我们发现的最大恒星之一的，是史蒂文森2-18。

blocks.en_text: It was probably born as a main sequence star a few tense of times the mass of the sun
blocks.zh_text: 它刚诞生时可能是一颗主序星，质量是太阳的几十倍，

blocks.en_text: And has likely lost about half its mass by now.
blocks.zh_text: 而到现在大概已经失去了一半的质量。

blocks.en_text: While typical red hypergiants are 1500 times the size of the sun,
blocks.zh_text: 典型的红超巨星有太阳的1500倍大，

blocks.en_text: the largest rough estimate places Stevenson 2-18 at 2150 solar radii.
blocks.zh_text: 而粗略估计的最大值，把史蒂文森2-18定在2150个太阳半径。

blocks.en_text: and shining with a list half a million times the power of the sun.
blocks.zh_text: 它的亮度大约是太阳的50万倍。

blocks.en_text: By comparison, the sun seems like a grain of dust.
blocks.zh_text: 相比之下，太阳就像一粒尘埃。

blocks.en_text: Our brains don't really have a way of grasping this kid of scale.
blocks.zh_text: 我们的大脑其实没办法真正理解这种尺度。

blocks.en_text: Even at light speed, it would take you 8.7 hours to travel around it once.
blocks.zh_text: 就算以光速飞行，绕它一圈也要8.7个小时。

blocks.en_text: The fastest plane on Earth would take about 500 yars.
blocks.zh_text: 地球上最快的飞机大约要飞500年。

blocks.en_text: Dropped on the sun, it would fill Saturn's orbit.
blocks.zh_text: 把它放到太阳的位置，它会填满土星的轨道。

blocks.en_text: As it evolves it will probably shed even more mass, and shrink into another, hotter hypergiant phase
blocks.zh_text: 随着它不断演化，它很可能会抛掉更多质量，收缩进入另一个更炽热的特超巨星阶段

blocks.en_text: Accumulate heavy elements in its core before finally exploding in a core collapse supernova,
blocks.zh_text: 在核心中积累重元素，最终以核心坍缩超新星的形式爆炸，

blocks.en_text: giving its gas back to the galaxy.
blocks.zh_text: 把它的气体还给星系。

blocks.en_text: This gas will then go on to form another generation of stars of all sizes,
blocks.zh_text: 这些气体随后会形成新一代各种大小的恒星，

blocks.en_text: starting the cycle of birth and death again, to light up our universe.
blocks.zh_text: 再次开启诞生与死亡的循环，照亮我们的宇宙。

blocks.en_text: Let's make this journey again, but this time, without the talking.
blocks.zh_text: 让我们再走一遍这段旅程，不过这次，不说话。

blocks.en_text: The universe is big.
blocks.zh_text: 宇宙很大。

blocks.en_text: There are many large things in it.
blocks.zh_text: 里面有很多巨大的东西。

blocks.en_text: If you want to play a bit more with size stuff, we have good news.
blocks.zh_text: 如果你想再多玩玩关于大小尺度的话题，我们有个好消息。

blocks.en_text: We've created our first app, Universe in a Nutshell, together with Tim Urban, the bring behind Wait but Why.
blocks.zh_text: 我们和Tim Urban一起做了我们的第一个应用，Universe in a Nutshell，他就是Wait but Why背后的那个人。

blocks.en_text: You can seamlessly travel between the smallest things in existence,
blocks.zh_text: 你可以在现存最小的东西之间无缝穿梭，

blocks.en_text: past the coronavirus,
blocks.zh_text: 经过冠状病毒，

blocks.en_text: human cell, and dinosaurs,
blocks.zh_text: 人体细胞和恐龙，

blocks.en_text: all the way to the largest star and galaxies,
blocks.zh_text: 一路到最大的恒星和星系，

blocks.en_text: and marvel at the whole observable universe.
blocks.zh_text: 惊叹于整个可观测宇宙。

blocks.en_text: You can learn more about each object, or simply enjoy the sheer scale of it all.
blocks.zh_text: 你可以了解每个物体的更多信息，或者单纯享受这一切的宏大尺度。

blocks.en_text: The app is inspired by the scale of the universe website by the Huang twins, that we spent a lot of time with when it came out years ago,
blocks.zh_text: 这个应用的灵感来自黄氏双胞胎做的scale of the universe网站，多年前它刚出来时我们花了很多时间在上面，

blocks.en_text: and felt that it was finally time to create a Wait but Why and Kurzgesagt version.
blocks.zh_text: 觉得终于该做一个Wait but Why和Kurzgesagt的版本了。

blocks.en_text: You can get it on your app store, there are no in-app purchases, and no ads.
blocks.zh_text: 你可以在应用商店里下载，没有应用内购买，也没有广告。

blocks.en_text: All future updates are included.
blocks.zh_text: 未来所有更新都包含在内。

blocks.en_text: And since this is our first app, we'd love to hear your feedback so we can improve it over time.
blocks.zh_text: 因为这是我们的第一个应用，我们很想听听你的反馈，好让我们不断改进它。

blocks.en_text: If this sounds good to you, download the Universe in a Nutshell app now, and leave us a 5 star review if you want to support it.
blocks.zh_text: 如果这听起来不错，现在就下载Universe in a Nutshell应用，如果你想支持它，就给我们留个五星好评。

blocks.en_text: Kurzgesagt and all the projects we do are mostly funded by viewers, like you.
blocks.zh_text: Kurzgesagt和我们做的所有项目，大部分都由像你这样的观众资助。

blocks.en_text: So if you like the app, we'll make more digital things in future.
blocks.zh_text: 所以如果你喜欢这个应用，我们以后会做更多数字产品。

blocks.en_text: Thank you for watching
blocks.zh_text: 感谢观看

blocks.en_text: [Outro music]
blocks.zh_text: [片尾音乐]
